texts: mixed: the role and the village link land, but "chief" is exposed as a free-standing property of Tessa Brae, which reads as her being a chief in general rather than chief *of the Feather-Collectors*; the compliant alternative buries "chief" inside one opaque role word, where nothing can ask who leads, and either way "the" (only one chief) is dropped. State the leadership as its own clause: "Tessa Brae is a Feather-Collector, and she leads the village's Feather-Collectors."

bad: two things go wrong. "The cliff base" is fused into a single kind, so the cliff itself never gets on record as the thing the base belongs to; and "during molting weeks" has no encodable form at all — a bare plural gives the translator no single stretch of time to hang the frame on, so the whole "during ..." clause has to be dropped and the seasonal restriction is lost. Rewrite as: "Tessa Brae walks the base of the cliff each morning during the molting season." — "the base of the cliff" introduces the cliff properly, and the singular "the molting season" gives the time frame something to be.

good. the pair of assistants is recorded as a counted group that also hands the walking down to each assistant, and "with Tessa Brae" makes her a co-walker rather than merging everyone into one event.
good. the change of role is recorded on Tessa Brae herself (she is the one who became it, and she now holds the role), and "nine years ago" is anchored as a measured gap back from now.
good. the state, its bearer, and what she is meticulous *about* are all kept, plus the plain "Tessa Brae is meticulous" form so a simple question about her still resolves.
